object_description: Three compact volumes linked by a central multipurpose hall
design_condition: The compact one-storey building is placed along the eastern edge, generating a well-sized schoolyard whose cuts establish neighborhood-scaled exterior zones, although the elongated extensions require fencing.

positive.statement: The compact building generates a schoolyard of beautiful size.
The cuts in the form give the outdoor spaces adequate proportions at neighborhood scale.
The building logically organizes three accesses as exterior extensions of the hall space.
The distribution of the different groups of premises is coherent.
The jury appreciated the architectural design, layout and general organization.
The supporting system provides good gravity-load descent and adequate seismic behavior.
The project meets fire quality assurance requirements.

negative.statement: The exterior extensions suffer from elongated proportions and require fences with a significant impact on the site.
The organizational plan loses clarity in the southern part where staff rooms extend the L-shaped plan.
The central gap is difficult to perceive and the jury has difficulty recognizing the theme of the world of childhood.
The central patio appears poorly sized, despite being necessary as a source of light.
The future expansion raises questions about the central location and reduced dimension of vertical circulation.
The project fails to convince with its identity inside and outside.
The heavy reinforced-concrete roof slab may require deep foundations on the poor-bearing-capacity soils.
A lightweight wooden roof would have better complemented the earthen walls and biosourced materials.
The project gives no indication of the planned extension.
